targetWords.definition: To abolish something means to put an end to it, such as a system or law.
targetWords.example: President Lincoln abolished slavery in the US.

targetWords.definition: To amend something means to change it to improve or make it accurate.
targetWords.example: The countries were in agreement that the treaty needed to be amended.

targetWords.definition: To aspire means to have a strong desire to achieve or do something.
targetWords.example: George aspired to be a doctor from a young age.

targetWords.definition: To censor information means to remove it if it is rude or rebellious.
targetWords.example: To protect innocent people, the location o f the bomb was censored. charter [tjaA a r] n.

targetWords.definition: constitution [kanstayu:Jan] n.
—►The country's constitution said a prime minister could only serve three terms.
targetWords.example: The country's constitution said a prime minister could only serve three terms.

targetWords.definition: When a place is cosmopolitan, it is full of people from many different places.
targetWords.example: There are dozens o f different types o f restaurants in a cosmopolitan city.

targetWords.definition: To disseminate information or knowledge means to distribute it.
targetWords.example: The organization disseminates information about the dangers o f smoking.

targetWords.definition: To flatter people means to praise them in an effort to please them.
targetWords.example: He was ju st flattering me when he said that my new dress looked gorgeous.

targetWords.definition: When someone is infamous, they are well known for something bad.
targetWords.example: That news channel is infamous for presenting biased information.

targetWords.definition: If one is lame, they cannot walk properly due to an injury to the leg or foot.
targetWords.example: The terrible accident left many people dead and several others lame.

targetWords.definition: To limp means to walk with difficulty because someone's leg or foot is hurt.
targetWords.example: After the injury, the player limped o ff o f the field.

targetWords.definition: An outburst is a sudden, strong expression of an emotion.
targetWords.example: ■ There was an outburst o f cheers when the comedian took the stage.

targetWords.definition: When a behavior is pathological, it is extreme, unacceptable, and uncontrollable.
targetWords.example: The pathological liar could not even tell the truth about unimportant matters.

targetWords.definition: When something is phenomenal, it is unusually great.
targetWords.example: The child's ability to play the piano is nothing short o f phenomenal. poll [poul] n.

targetWords.definition: —►The p oll showed that many people support the plan to stop gang violence.
targetWords.example: The p oll showed that many people support the plan to stop gang violence.

targetWords.definition: Remorse is a strong feeling of sadness and regret.
targetWords.example: When I realized what I did, I felt remorse for my actions.

targetWords.definition: Secrecy is the behavior of keeping things secret.
targetWords.example: The secrecy o f the big organization made the government nervous.

targetWords.definition: To tackle something means to deal with it in a determined and efficient way.

story.title: The Mayor of Sherman
story.passage:
The cosmopolitan city of Sherman needed to elect a new mayor. Two men aspired to

become mayor: Mr. Jones and Mr. Webb. Mr. Jones was a tall, handsome man. He was a

phenomenal speaker, and the citizens loved him. However, Mr. Jones didn't know much

about running a city. He was a pathological liar who merely flattered people with his words.

Mr. Webb was very different. He was a small, unattractive man. He was lame and limped

when he walked. But he was an expert on politics and knew what was best for the people.

The citizens of Sherman didn't care about what the politicians had to say.

No one listened to Mr. Webb, even though he had great ideas. They cheered

when Mr. Jones spoke, although he didn't talk about important things. His

pretty words put people in a trance. All the polls predicted that Mr. Jones

would win the election.

When the votes were totaled, Mr. Jones won easily.

But when he took office, he didn't know what

to do! He tried to hide his ignorance by

working in secrecy. He added a law to the

city's constitution that prevented citizens

from seeing the mayor. He even

censored newspapers that tried

to disseminate information

about his inability to help

the people.

Soon, however, Mr.

Jones became infamous

for his poor leadership.

There was an outburst of

anger among the citizens. They

were full of remorse for their

misguided decision to elect an

ignorant mayor. They voted to remove

Mr. Jones and let Mr. Webb take over.

Immediately, Mr. Webb proved that

he was a great mayor. He abolished

Mr. Jones's law, and he was willing

to talk openly with everyone. He

tackled important issues and

amended unfair laws in the city's

charter.

The citizens learned that a

pleasant appearance and nice

words do not make a good leader.

The most important qualities are

intelligence and a desire to help

others.
